name: Consolidation and learning
summary: The dream pass that turns signals into rules, its owner and agent, the preference lifecycle, lessons and decision models.

features.name: Dream consolidation pass
features.summary: Promotes repeated signals to rules, confirms, quarantines and retires them by evidence, and replays missed days.
capabilities: Creates a topic's unconfirmed rule when one sign leads by 3 signals in 14 days; guardrails can add minimums
Confirms on first applied evidence in 14 days; quarantines a confirmed rule once violated >= applied > 2
Retires on trial expiry, rebuttal, a violation in quarantine, an outdated event or 90 days without evidence
Scores confidence as the Wilson 95% lower bound of the applied share times linear freshness over 90 days
Queues a model-written rollup when 20 new facts or 5 new rollups gather (rollup thresholds)
Replays each missed UTC day as its own window, so a pass after a silence ends where daily passes would
Starts at the first session of a day on the owner's device (`dream.auto`)
Previews a pass by dry run, staged bundle, intent review, review candidates or retention review
Waits up to 2 minutes for a busy store lock (its session's take and answer too); hooks and tools keep 5 s
Ends incomplete (exit 0) if a busy lock stops it after it queued work; with none, or twice in a row, fails
limits: Once a store brain has a dream owner, only that device runs live passes; other machines run dry runs only
The pass writes no model text itself; rollup summaries and topic wording wait in the dream work queue
Missed-day replay needs a brain served from the brain store; a legacy `Brain/` tree runs one window
Automatic start needs a session start hook or the MCP server on the owner's machine, else `dream run`

features.name: Cross-topic rule generalization
features.summary: Optionally promotes one rule a day per owner from confirmed rules that repeat across topics, citing each source.
capabilities: Compares confirmed rules across topic buckets only, pairing principles at Jaccard 0.6+ (`cross_topic.jaccard`)
Fires on a cluster that spans at least 2 distinct topics (`cross_topic.min_topics`, never below 2)
Writes one unconfirmed inferred rule per owner a day, with evidence links to every source rule
Promotes only clusters whose source rules share one owner, so one agent's rules never shape another's
Keeps the daily allowance in a ledger, `Brain/cross-topic-rules.json` or the store's dream-replay records
limits: Off unless `cross_topic.enabled` is true; with the block absent the dream pass is unchanged
Never modifies or retires the source rules; the new rule then confirms or retires like any other
Topic-keyed recall does not find the new rule; its evidence links and lineage lead to it
Has no verb or tool of its own; it runs inside the dream pass

features.name: Dream owner
features.summary: One device and agent run the live dream passes for a brain; other machines preview, and the role can move.
capabilities: Keeps one owner (a device and its agent) per brain, folded from claim, request and release store records
Refuses a live pass on any other device with dream_not_owner before any model call or write; dry runs pass
Binds the installation that creates the brain as its owner when its agent name is known
Moves the role by a request that the owner's device grants at its next look
Settles concurrent first claims by the lowest (clock, device), so every device folds the same owner
Shows other machines one line a day when the owner has covered no window for 3 days
Sets primary_agent with brain set-primary, which renames the owner's agent when run on the owner's device
limits: Needs the brain store: a brain with no owner record or a legacy `Brain/` tree runs live passes anywhere
The gate is the device: any agent on the owner's device may run a live pass
The MCP tool cannot force a takeover and moves the role only at local reach
On a store brain with a dream owner, `brain set-primary` refuses on any device that is not the owner

features.name: Dream agent and work queue
features.summary: Model work of a dream pass waits in a queue for the operator's own agent command, which is set and verified per machine.
capabilities: Holds model work as store records with 15-minute leases, backoff from 1 min to 6 h, parking after 5 failures
An active decision model takes closed questions of its non-off uses; the agent command gets all other work
Starts the configured command without a shell, filling {prompt}, {mcp_config}, {mcp_command}, {mcp_args_json}
Gives the session one MCP server with take, answer and finish tools, bound to the run by a hashed token
Uses a command only after agent check answered two canary items in a throwaway store within 120 s
Gives the agent dream_agent_budget_ms (300 s) per pass; at the deadline it ends the session's process tree
Caps a session at dream_agent_items (100); one that meets it is followed by another while work and time last
Hands a session up to dream_agent_batch (10) items per take, and as many per answer call
Tries one dream_agent_fallbacks entry when a session fails to start, exits with an error or answers nothing
Marks the session process so hooks capture nothing and no dream pass starts inside it
limits: No presets ship; each machine sets a full command, and the command is never synced
The model recorded with an answer is the session's own statement and is not checked
A session sees private items unless `dream_agent_private` is off
Queue retry and cancel write only on the dream owner's device

features.name: Dream drafts review
features.summary: Model-written text from a dream pass records its agent and model and can be held for operator approval.
capabilities: Records on every text answer the agent that answered and the model its session named
Writes a rollup summary under Brain/rollups/ with written_by, written_by_model and written_by_item fields
Creates a topic from an applied wording with the answering agent, model and queue item in its record
Holds text answers in awaiting-review when dream.apply_drafts is review; auto, the default, applies them
Applies an approved held answer at the next pass (`dream queue approve`)
Closes a rejected held answer with its reason and writes nothing (`dream queue reject`)
Skips the rollup write on a re-apply when the note's written_by_item already names that queue item
limits: Review covers text work only (rollup summaries, topic wording); closed-question answers apply directly
Approve and reject write only on the dream owner's device

features.name: Preference lifecycle
features.summary: Reads, pins, rejects, merges and expires preferences, with their evidence trail and an audit of content changes.
capabilities: Looks up one preference with its evidence trail, everything on a topic, or log events since a time
Answers a topic query as of a past instant (--at) or with lapsed memories kept (--show-expired)
Pins a rule against stale, expiry, rebuttal and quarantine retires; an outdated event still retires it
Retires a rule as user-rejected with a reason that suppresses later signals on its topic and scope
Merges two same-topic, same-scope rules: unions evidence, sums counters, retires the dropped one as merged
Sets, changes or clears the expiration_date of a signal or preference by id
Audits each mutation (agent, reason, revision, hash) as per-device JSONL or a store row; skips no-op updates
Keeps a per-field before and after edit history beside each preference (brain history)
limits: Merge takes only confirmed or quarantined rules of one topic and scope, and takes no snapshot
Merge refuses a pinned drop into an unpinned keep; the pinned rule must be the keep
Merge leaves confidence to the next dream pass; `--force` skips only the name-aware entity guard
Pin, unpin, reject, merge and history are CLI verbs; MCP has query, expire and audit

features.name: Corrections and supersession
features.summary: Tombstones, supersedes or time-replaces any memory and reports the blast radius of a correction first.
capabilities: Tombstones a memory of any type in place with a reason; recall, injection and dream skip it, bytes stay
Supersedes a predecessor through a `superseded_by` link that recall resolves to the live tip
Replaces a fact at one instant: closes `valid_until` and opens `valid_from`, both written or neither
Previews a correction's blast radius by default: claim-graph closure, wikilink mentions, ledger claims
Applies a correction with `--apply`, closing validity at the window end or tombstoning a flatly wrong memory
Retires a signal with a reason, out of dream input but still searchable (`brain signal retire`)
Lists memories injected but never used, contradicted or heavily used, from observed-use verdicts
Proposes missing `superseded_by` back-links on retired rules that an active rule supersedes
limits: `brain semantics-backfill` only previews; it has no apply path
Wikilink retargeting never rewrites `Brain/log` or receipt lines
A target outside the caller's read reach is refused as missing before any write

features.name: Lessons for agent rule files
features.summary: Scores outcome-tagged lessons into a digest and promotes approved ones into managed blocks of agent rule files.
capabilities: Folds dead-end notes and applied, violated and outdated evidence into one signed digest, Brain/lessons.md
Decays each result with a 30-day half-life (lessons.half_life_days), so fresh outcomes outweigh old ones
Tiers lessons preferred (2+ applied artifacts, no negatives), tentative, contested (both signs ever) or avoid
Regenerates the digest after every dream pass, top 20 by decayed salience (lessons.limit)
Qualifies a lesson for promotion only from a confirmed, high-confidence, preferred rule in an enabled scope
Pins each operator approval to the rule text's hash; a changed rule leaves the block until approved again
Writes an approved lesson as a managed block into AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md with `--apply`
Lists promotion candidates, each blocked one with its reason (`lessons candidates`)
limits: Promotion is off until the machine config key `lessons.promotion.scopes` names a scope
Only the CLI approves or denies; no MCP tool, hook or dream path promotes a lesson
Dead-end lessons never promote; only preference-derived lessons reach rules files
Targets only the instruction files at the vault root

features.name: Decision models
features.summary: An optional typed judgment model that reranks, filters and checks candidates; each use runs off, shadow or enforce.
capabilities: Asks yes/no, choice (up to 255 options) or score (2 to 10 levels) questions and gets probabilities, no text
Runs each of 17 uses (rerank, skills, dedup, topic routing, recall filter) as off, shadow or enforce
Tries an ordered provider chain in one timeout budget (3 s default), failing over only on network or timeout
Stops sending once the day's spend reaches decision_model_cost_gate_usd (0.5 USD by default)
Lets private records out only for the 9 topic and context uses, on an all-local chain or via private_uses
Records one accounting row per request (provider, model, outcome, latency, tokens, cost) for the report
Runs preregistered evals for rerank and recall_inject with real spend; promote writes a machine tuning mark
Fits per-model thresholds for dedup, tension, labels, extract_prefilter at 5% false actions (8+ samples)
limits: Off unless enabled with a provider whose key variable is set, or a keyless loopback server
The deterministic result stays canonical; a failed, gated or off call returns it unchanged
A vault can opt out with `decision_model.enabled: false`; endpoints and keys are machine settings
The `llm-emulation` adapter's probabilities are uncalibrated, and it is used only when named

features.name: Judgment commands
features.summary: Hands a judgment call to an operator-configured command as JSON on stdin and reads its JSON verdict back.
capabilities: Sends one question as JSON on stdin to a configured shell command and reads one JSON answer from stdout
Serves the benchmark judge (`bench_judge_cmd`) and the hygiene conflict resolver (`hygiene.resolver_cmd`)
Serves the skill rewrite judge (`skill_rewrite_judge_cmd`)
Treats an unset command as skipped, and a nonzero exit, a signal, a timeout or bad JSON as an error result
Ends a command after 60 seconds by default
limits: Bench and skill-rewrite verdicts are advisory; a resolver_cmd merge or supersede verdict drives hygiene apply
Open Second Brain runs no model here; every command is the operator's own
